title: the lac house
hook: as the Pandavas leave, Vidura warns Yudhishthira in words nobody else can follow, and in Varanavata the new house smells wrong
carry: this house is made to burn

segments.voice: Yesterday, the lac house was planned: a holiday offered, a blind king persuaded. A trap made of kindness.

A farewell at the edge of the city. The Pandavas and their mother are setting out for Varanavata, and an unhappy crowd has followed them out. Vidura, their uncle, walks beside Yudhishthira and says something strange, in a tongue the crowd doesn't understand, the text says, that only Yudhishthira can follow. To anyone listening, it sounds like a riddle. To Yudhishthira, it's a warning.
screen: `A FAREWELL AT THE CITY'S EDGE.` → `VIDURA SPEAKS IN A HIDDEN TONGUE.` → `A WARNING IN PLAIN SIGHT.`

segments.voice: Vidura's riddle goes something like this. There's a weapon not made of steel that can still destroy a body; whoever knows it can't be killed by it. A fire that burns a whole forest can't reach the creatures that live in holes underground. Someone who knows the roads, who can find the way by the stars, will survive. Fire, holes, roads, stars. Yudhishthira answers simply: I have understood. Later, on the road, Kunti asks what all that was about, and he tells her: Vidura was warning us of fire. Then they arrive. Varanavata welcomes them with joy. Purochana greets them warmly, and after some days moves them into the new house. Walking through it, Yudhishthira catches a smell: fat, and lac. He turns to Bhima. This house, he says, is made to burn. Now step back and look at the week. Karna gave away his armor. He walked into an arena where only his mother knew him. He was crowned and mocked in a single afternoon. Then a plot was laid, and a warning given in words no one else could read. A week of hidden things: a hidden brother, a hidden grief, a hidden trap, a hidden message. The Mahabharata keeps letting the listener in on secrets the characters don't share. Today, at least, one hidden thing is caught in time.
screen: `FIRE, HOLES, ROADS, STARS.` · `I HAVE UNDERSTOOD.` · `THE HOUSE SMELLS OF LAC.` · `A WEEK OF HIDDEN THINGS.` · then, large: `THIS HOUSE IS MADE TO BURN.`

segments.voice: Recall a warning someone once gave you, gently, maybe sideways, that you only understood later. If thanks rises for them, even if you didn't listen, let it. Then rest, and notice the room you're in, its sounds and smells, the way Yudhishthira noticed his.
Vidura, the uncle whose riddle of fire, holes, roads and stars warned Yudhishthira the new house was built to burn.
Your line: this house is made to burn. A riddle, understood in time. That's day seven hundred thirty-five.

howItsDone: Vidura is honored in Hindu tradition as a figure of wisdom and good counsel, and his coded warning at Varanavata is one of the scenes told to show it.

fork.setup: you're Yudhishthira. your uncle has just warned you in riddles of fire and holes in the ground. the crowd is watching. what do you do?
options: ask him to say it plainly.
fork.reveal: he answers: I have understood. he explains it to Kunti later, on the road, and goes on to Varanavata.

original.note: Sanskrit vidura: the name of the Pandavas' wise uncle who sends the warning.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Pandavas walk into the trap without a clue.
what it means: Vidura warns Yudhishthira in a hidden tongue, and he recognizes the house by its smell.
what a scholar hears: the riddle's images, a weapon not of steel, a fire that can't reach creatures in holes, point ahead to how the brothers will survive.

chat.says: Why did Vidura speak to Yudhishthira in a riddle?
options: So the crowd couldn't follow; only Yudhishthira understood the warning.
He was testing whether Yudhishthira was wise enough to be king.
It was a farewell blessing for a safe journey and a happy festival.
chat.meaning: Vidura used a tongue only Yudhishthira could follow, so the warning stayed hidden: fire, holes, roads, stars. Yudhishthira understood.

Vidura.meaning: the maid's son, wise in dharma, uncle to the cousins

Varanavata.meaning: the town where the Pandavas were sent

Yudhishthira.meaning: the eldest Pandava, son of Dharma

Purochana.meaning: Duryodhana's minister, who built the house to burn

Kunti.meaning: Pandu's first wife, who chose him at her self-choice

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Jatugriha Parva (Vidura's warning in a hidden tongue; Yudhishthira's reply; arrival at Varanavata; Yudhishthira recognizes the house)

notes: All paraphrase. Ganguli calls Vidura's language the Mlechchha tongue; the script says only 'a tongue only Yudhishthira can follow' to avoid an unexplained term. A Keeper may prefer to name it.
